text: The Privacy Act applies to personal information held by private companies in Canada.
Under the Privacy Act, personal information shall not be collected by a government institution unless it relates directly to an operating program or activity of the institution.
Every Canadian citizen and permanent resident has a right to access their own personal information held by a government institution under the Privacy Act.
Under the Privacy Act, personal information may be used by a government institution for any government purpose, regardless of the original purpose of collection.
The Privacy Act defines personal information to include information about an identifiable individual that is recorded in any form.
Under the Privacy Act, the Federal Court is the court with jurisdiction in Privacy Act matters.
The Privacy Act requires government institutions to collect personal information directly from the individual wherever possible.
Under the Privacy Act, a government institution may disclose personal information without consent under any circumstances it deems appropriate.
